title.narrative: Emergency response for IDPs and vulnerable families in Gaza

description.narrative: ltpgtThis Action seeks to enhance the safety, dignity, and physical protection of conflict-affected households in the Middle Area- Dier Al Balah and southern Gaza- Khan Younes, Mawasi Area through the provision of emergency shelter assistance. By distributing Sealing-off Kits (SOK), and framing materials. In addition to seasonal bedding sets and clothing kits (for both winter and summer), the project aims to significantly improve the living conditions and meet the essential needs of displaced populations in the informal IDP sites. Addressing urgent shelter needs is critical for increasing resilience and reducing reliance on negative coping mechanisms. ltbrgtThe Shelter Non-Food Items (NFIs) will be procured externally by NRC and delivered to Gaza. Project participants will be selected based on an assessment of shelter needs and specific vulnerabilities, while the prioritization ofsites will follow NRC site management criteria, the field assessment will be conducted by NRC local partner “Beit Lahia Development Association (BLDA)”, and the data analysis and selection of project participants will be validated with the NRC team. ltbrgtNRC will manage the distribution process in full support of BLDA field staff. BLDA –in cooperation with the NRC site management team-will coordinate closely with targeted sites and beneficiaries to streamline the distribution process and ensure communicating information about the distribution and CFM. For individuals encountering obstacles in reaching the distribution points, BLDA will provide transportation and labor to deliver the shelter items directly to their homes, ensuring equitable access to assistance and reducing potential barriers, especially for vulnerable groups such as the elderly, disabled, or those in remote areas. In addition, BLDA will hire skilled labour to install the framing materials and the sealing of kits for those lacking the experience or the capacity to do it themselves. ltbrgtA Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercise will be conducted by NRC MEL unit to assess the impact of the action and inform adjustments to current and future interventions.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtUnder this project, NRC will focus on assisting 16,520 individuals (2950 households) among the most vulnerable people living in the IDP informal sites within the humanitarian zones of Deir El Balah and the western areas of Khan Younes. The selection of IDP sites will be based on established site management criteria, prioritizing those with limited access to humanitarian support. Within these sites, the shelter team will utilize a combination of socio-economic and shelter criteria to identify the most vulnerable households at risk of harsh weather conditions. The distribution of sealing-off materials will prioritize families without shelters or those living in deteriorating makeshifts that are not protected against rainwater or wind. Families affected by shelling due to military operations, and those who have suffered fire accidents that damaged their tents or makeshift. Furthermore, providing bedding sets and clothing kits will focus on individuals experiencing severe socio-economic vulnerability or protection concerns identified during assessments.ltbrgtlt/pgt
